get_ce_value

Source: R/finance.R
get_ce_value.Rd

Certainty-equivalent evaluation of the initial (flat -> tou/dynamic) switching decision, using the five costs from get_prospect_costs() and the household's prospect-theory parameters.

get_ce_value(
  scen,
  flat,
  tou_noflex,
  tou_flex,
  det_noflex,
  det_flex,
  flex_certainty_tou = 0.8,
  flex_certainty_det = 0.7,
  lambda = 2.25
)

Arguments

scen

scenario dataframe source of the pt_* prospect-theory parameters, including the plan-specific certainty-of-flex values (pt_certainty_flex_tou, pt_certainty_flex_det)

flat

annual cost on the flat tariff

tou_noflex

annual cost on tou, unshifted load

tou_flex

annual cost on tou, optimally shifted load

det_noflex

annual cost on dynamic, unshifted load

det_flex

annual cost on dynamic, optimally shifted load

flex_certainty_tou

flexibility outcome confidence tou

flex_certainty_det

flexibility outcome confidence det

lambda

loss aversion (median 2.25)

Value

a list: flat, certainty_tou, CE_tou, CE_bill_tou, certainty_det, CE_det, CE_bill_det

Details

For each of tou and dynamic, this treats switching as a two-outcome prospect relative to the flat-tariff reference bill: a "flex" outcome (the household achieves its optimal load-shifted cost) and a "noflex" outcome (it doesn't, and pays the unshifted cost instead), each weighted by the plan's pt_certainty_flex_* probability. The Kahneman-Tversky value function (curvature pt_alpha/pt_beta, loss aversion pt_loss_aversion) and probability weighting function (pt_prob_weight_gains/pt_prob_weight_losses) convert that into a Prospect Value, which is then inverted back into a euro-denominated Certainty Equivalent the guaranteed saving a household would consider exactly as good as the actual uncertain prospect.

Examples

prices_scen <- set_prices(sD)
params <- scenario_params(sD,2032)
#costs <- get_prospect_costs_light(sD,8760, 0.4, 5, 0.3, 48, "LP1", 2025, prices_scen,params)
#get_ce_value(sD,costs$flat, costs$tou_noflex, costs$tou_flex, costs$det_noflex, costs$det_flex,0.8,0.7,2.25)
